industry.capacity: India's refining capacity is ~258 MMTPA; BPCL's three refineries (Mumbai 12, Kochi 15.5, Bina 7.8 MMTPA) are ~14% of it and ran at 116% utilisation in FY26 (41.15 MMT). BPCL sold 54.18 MMT in India in FY26, 27.3% of PSU sales, and needs more product than it refines: ~80% of the fuel it sells comes from its own refineries.
industry.demand: Petroleum product demand grows ~2.5-3.5% a year; BPCL's domestic sales grew 3.5% in FY26 (petrol +5.7%, diesel +1%, jet fuel +11.4%) and 0.3% YoY in Q1FY27 (LPG −21% on supply curbs; petrol +8%, diesel +8%).
industry.pricing: Petrol and diesel are formally deregulated but in practice priced by the three PSU marketers with the Government's consent; household LPG is regulated and its losses are compensated case by case (₹7,594 cr approved for BPCL in Oct-2025, paid in 12 monthly instalments from Nov-2025).
industry.war2026: US-Iran conflict from end-Feb 2026: Strait of Hormuz disrupted. The Government cut SAED on petrol and diesel by ₹10/litre on 27-Mar-2026 and re-imposed export duties; retail prices were raised in tranches only from the second half of May. BPCL's crude premium over the Indian basket widened from US$4-5/bbl to >US$15/bbl; landed crude reached Brent + US$10-12 in May.

competition: IOC (largest refiner and marketer, ~42% of petroleum sales) and HPCL are the other two PSU marketers; prices move together. Reliance and Nayara are private, export-oriented refiners with smaller retail networks; MRPL and CPCL are standalone refiners. BPCL has the highest fuel-station productivity of the three (139 KL per outlet per month in FY26 vs ~120-125 at HPCL and IOC, per the July-2026 presentation) and a smaller, more complex refining base than IOC.

excluded.HINDPETRO: Earnings distorted on 30-Sep-2026: HPCL has the highest marketing-to-refining ratio of the three OMCs, so the Q1FY27 marketing loss collapsed its trailing EBITDA and its trailing EV/EBITDA is far above its five-year median, which is not a re-rating (same exclusion as in the published IOC report). Shown with HPCL as a sensitivity row.

peers.note: OMC/refiner set as set by the published IOC report, with IOC now a peer and BPCL itself excluded. Three usable names (IOC, MRPL, CPCL), the minimum under the thin-peer-set rule; the widened oil & gas set is a sensitivity. Measured on EV/EBITDA (our primary method).

street.methodView: The street values BPCL on a sum of the parts: EV/EBITDA of the refining and marketing business (5.5-6.5x on Dec-27E to FY28E; Emkay 5.8x Jun-28E) plus investments at a 20-30% discount to market and upstream at a discount to transaction or book value (Motilal Oswal, JM, Emkay, Antique), or on P/B (PL 1.2x FY28E). We follow the EV/EBITDA sum of the parts and show P/E and DCF as cross-checks.

governance.board: Chairman and Managing Director Sanjay Khanna (Director Refineries; additional charge of CMD from 1-May-2025); Director (Finance) V.R.K. Gupta. As a Maharatna CPSE, BPCL's board is appointed by the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; the statutory auditors are appointed by the C&AG.
governance.independentDirectors: No independent directors: the last three ceased on 27-Mar-2026 and another on 10-Mar-2026; the Audit Committee existed only until 27-Mar-2026 and is to be reconstituted when the Government appoints independent directors. The auditors flagged the non-compliance in the Q1FY27 results; no woman director during the period.
governance.pricing: Retail petrol, diesel and LPG prices are set in consultation with the Government; minority shareholders bear under-recoveries until (and unless) compensated.
governance.relatedParty: Large purchases from associates and JVs: Petronet LNG ₹6,669 cr, IGL ₹1,768 cr, Sabarmati Gas ₹647 cr in FY26.

moat: Three complex refineries (Nelson 9.8-11.8) that process 76% high-sulphur crude, a coastal location (Mumbai, Kochi) and pipelines, and the most productive fuel-station network of the PSU three. These lower costs and lift GRMs (premium to Singapore for four years), but do not protect margins: prices are administered and the Government decides when OMCs absorb losses.
critiques: Marketing margins are a policy variable: in FY23 and Q1FY27 retail prices were held while crude spiked; BPCL's implied marketing margin swung from +₹5.8/litre (Q4FY26) to −₹5.4/litre (Q1FY27).
A new capex cycle (₹1.7 lakh cr plan: Bina petchem ₹49,800 cr, PRFCC, Kochi PP, upstream, and possibly a ~₹95,000 cr Andhra refinery) will keep free cash flow thin and returns lower.
Upstream has destroyed value so far: Brazil impaired by ₹1,774 cr (FY25) and ₹4,349 cr (FY26) at standalone level; Mozambique was under force majeure from 2021 to Nov-2025.
Q1FY27 consolidated loss is flattered by a ₹1,885 cr one-off FCTR gain; standalone lost ₹3,962 cr.
Governance: no independent directors and no Audit Committee since Mar-2026.
